findings.title: Global data law compliance without assessment
findings.deviation: The contract requires AtliQ to comply with UAE and Oman data protection laws (for the Dubai and Muscat properties) without an accompanying Data Processing Agreement or a cross-border transfer assessment.
findings.impact: AtliQ may be held to data processing and security standards in foreign jurisdictions for which its Indian operations have not been legal-audited or technically prepared.
findings.quote: AtliQ shall process personal data contained in Client Data only for the purposes of the Pilot and in accordance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and any other applicable data protection law, including the laws applicable to Properties located outside India.
findings.counterPosition: Limit processing obligations to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and agree to execute a specific DPA for non-Indian jurisdictions only after a technical and legal assessment of cross-border data transfer requirements.

fine.note: Liquidated damages are correctly capped at 5% of the milestone fee, exclude client-caused delay, and are the sole remedy for delay.
The aggregate liability cap is mutual and set at 1x fees, with standard carve-outs for fraud and wilful misconduct.
Mutual indemnity for negligence and breach is standard; note that IP infringement is safely included under the general liability cap.
Ownership of specific deliverables transfers to the client only upon payment, and AtliQ retains all background IP and tools.
The 30-day convenience termination notice is reasonable and ensures AtliQ is paid for pro-rata work in progress.
Confidentiality terms are mutual with a standard 3-year survival period and appropriate exclusions.
The performance warranty is standard and includes a clear 30-day window for correcting any material non-conformities.
The agreement contains no non-compete or non-solicit restrictions on AtliQ.
The payment terms (30 days) and dispute resolution process for invoices align with the playbook.
